summary: Opened the question of whether a restart reconstructs a node's own configuration from its committed log, promoted four source-grounded behaviours (NewRaft's configuration scan starts above max(lastSnapshotIndex,lastApplied); restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied before that scan; the reconstructed configuration drives the node's own election gating, quorumSize and leader commitment; duplicate AppendEntries are skipped so a healthy leader does not repair it), registered one necessary gap about a repair path, and requested one focused multi-case probe that contrasts RestoreCommittedLogs enabled/disabled across a no-snapshot and a snapshot-then-remove single-voter restart shape, recording the reconstructed configuration, its snapshot origin, election attempts and bounded leadership recovery. Construction-time local feedback in the draft workspace matched the prediction (flag on: latest configuration index 0 with an empty server set and no election attempt, or index 1 equal to the snapshot's two-voter configuration while the committed single-voter entry at index 103 was skipped, ~40 pre-vote campaigns and no leader in 3000 ms; flag off: correct index and prompt leadership), but the retained receipt is still outstanding, so the account and defect judgment remain unresolved. Local build scratch (draft/tmp/gocache, draft/tmp/localrun) was removed; the draft keeps update.json and the validated harness assurance_generated_test.go.
